what_it_does: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are AI models that learn from data structured as a graph — think social networks, molecule graphs, or road maps — by repeatedly passing information between connected nodes through many layers. Training a deep GNN (many layers) across a cluster of GPUs is slow because the standard approach splits the graph across machines, requiring enormous amounts of data to be shipped between GPUs for every training step, and that communication cost grows with both graph size and depth. Mithril instead assigns each GPU a different set of consecutive GNN layers rather than a different piece of the graph, so each GPU processes every node but only through its slice of layers. This collapses the cross-machine communication by roughly one factor per layer. A pipelining scheme keeps all GPUs busy simultaneously, and a speculative forward-pass trick breaks dependency chains between graph chunks. A hybrid mode can combine both strategies for very large graphs.
